upstreamMaintenanceAndSecurityNotes.note: Tink 1.4.0 fixed a potential AES-GCM-HKDF Streaming segment-counter overflow after more than 2^32 segments in Java and Go.
upstreamMaintenanceAndSecurityNotes.candidateAssessment: v1.23.0 postdates the fix; protocol caps and reviewer analysis still required.

upstreamMaintenanceAndSecurityNotes.note: Tink Java 1.17.0 fixed excessive memory use in HKDF caused by asynchronously cleaned direct buffers.
upstreamMaintenanceAndSecurityNotes.candidateAssessment: v1.23.0 postdates the fix; memory behavior is not benchmarked by this package.

upstreamMaintenanceAndSecurityNotes.note: Tink Java 1.18.0 changed AndroidKeystore AEAD behavior on API 28 and older for inputs larger than 128 KiB from producing invalid ciphertext to throwing.
upstreamMaintenanceAndSecurityNotes.candidateAssessment: v1.23.0 postdates the fix; the planned design wraps small key material rather than bulk recovery data and requires key-loss tests.

templateAndProtocolRisks.risk: Streaming EOF can be confused with authentication/truncation failure if the recovery API contract is handled incorrectly.
AES-GCM streaming security requires unique key and nonce-prefix combinations and no rewrite at the same segment position under the same key.
StreamingAeadKeyTemplates is deprecated in v1.23.0 and its static helper pulls in broad protobuf/key-type code.
Authenticated manifest encoding, anti-rollback generation binding and microfile AEAD template are not yet selected.

limitations: An empty exact-version advisory query is not proof of absence of vulnerabilities.
GitHub advisory package mapping does not list historical Android-coordinate issues consistently; upstream release notes were reviewed separately.
The snapshot does not approve the crypto template, recovery protocol, dependency or production use.
A fresh advisory scan and exact future resolved-graph review are required immediately before any authorized execution.
